To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present TVM, an open source compiler infrastructure for performance portability of deep learning models across a wide range of hardware platforms.
TVM provides performance portability to diverse deep learning hardware back ends by providing a unified graph level and operator-level optimization stack.
we propose TVM, a new end to end optimization framework that provides performance portability to a wide range of deep learning workloads and hardware back ends.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can we provide a common compiler infrastructure that enables performance portability for deep learning across hardware back ends?
the following questions: (1) How to provide a portable compiler for deep learning workloads that can target arbitrary hardware back ends?

the following: - How to expose graph level optimizations to deep learning work loads. - How to target diverse hardware back ends (CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerations) with a single compiler infrastructure. - How to enable memory reuse and latency hiding in deep learning operators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TVM provides performance portability for deep learning workloads.
TVM enables deep learning workloads to run across diverse hardware platforms, with performance that is competitive with state of art libraries, with minimal effort.
TVM is a comprehensive, end-to-end deep learning compiler infrastructure that provides high performance across diverse hardware backends.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TVM provides an open source end to end optimization framework that delivers performance portability to a diverse set of hardware back ends for deep learning workloads.
we provide a unified framework to optimize the deep learning workloads for a variety of hardware back ends.
we have developed an end to end stack that allows us to compile deep learning workloads for arbitrary hardware back ends.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TVM stack is a general framework for deep learning workloads and can provide performance portability for deep learning work loads across diverse hardware backends.

the performance portability of deep learning workloads to new hardware back ends is achievable by exposing the graph level and operator optimizations to the user and providing a high level of abstraction to target diverse hardware back ends.
a unified optimization framework is necessary to provide high level of performance portability to diverse hardware targets.
